subject: quant-ph
title_original: Coexistence of dipolar and quadrupolar higher-order topology
authors: Konstantin Rodionenko, Maxim Mazanov, Maxim A. Gorlach
abstract: Two-dimensional higher-order topological insulators are typically classified either as dipolar or quadrupolar depending on the relevant invariant. These two classes were previously considered non-overlapping. Here we put forward an example system exhibiting dipolar and quadrupolar higher-order topology simultaneously, suggest its implementation using the arrays of laser-written evanescently coupled optical waveguides and support our conclusions by the full-wave numerical simulations.
title_relatable: Two 'incompatible' quantum phases found living together in one material
hook: A photonic waveguide array defies classification by hosting two supposedly mutually exclusive topological phases at once.
summary: Two types of higher-order topological insulator — dipolar and quadrupolar — were thought to be mutually exclusive, like odd and even numbers. This work shows a single system can host both simultaneously, demonstrated through a design using laser-written optical waveguides confirmed by full numerical simulation. It forces a rethink of how these exotic phases are catalogued and opens new possibilities for engineering protected boundary states.
